scope: Host evidence summary for parent #615 documentation; no production implementation verdict beyond the explicitly narrowed configuration.
narrow_configuration: Bitwig Studio6.1/macOS,44.1kHz, three CLAP tuner sources and one CLAP Master hub in the tested shared process grouping, fixed graph with verified source offsets, keep_alive=true, fixed128/512/1024-sample activation bounds, D2048, explicitly measured lifecycle resets. Vital receiving requires the tested host/plugin MPE and48-semitone range settings.

rows.evidence: Runs09-11,23: independently timed callback pairing and reinserted instances support a common raw engine counter in this fixture. Calibrated B+64 aligns all five three-source musical cohorts exactly; every accepted assignment has all source intervals complete.
rows.limit: Raw counter equality alone is insufficient; branch PDC can move musical input times. Fixed measured offsets only; no automatic calibration or arbitrary graph changes.

rows.case: Round trip, D and callback bounds
rows.evidence: Runs05-07: RT/offline at128/512/1024; accepted events preserve D2048 and durations. Run24 calibrated boundary replies are visible one or two source callbacks later; healthy minimum deadline margin is1021samples (raw offset1021), with1023sample margin at exact last1023.
rows.limit: Every activation reported min=max. Short or variable enclosing host callbacks remain unobserved; different buffer/sample-rate configurations are outside the measured scope. D2048 is a conservative measured candidate, not a proven minimum or future scheduling guarantee.

rows.evidence: Run18 actual64-sample automation splits and callback-boundary crossing; run21 gives345 callbacks per pass with distinct subblocks sharing local8; run24 accepts raw offset0 and exact last1023, with identity/tuning preserved.
rows.limit: Transport event offsets remain0. No intra-callback transport-event split; no exact local63 of a64-sample subblock. Equal-offset case is measured at local8, not local0.

rows.case: Playback, stopped live, loop and seek
rows.evidence: Runs18-19: song wraps with continuous raw sample clock; held notes released at4s loop boundary. One stopped live note at offset0 is accepted at D and its audio returns to zero. Manual transport jumps are recorded.
rows.limit: Measured manual seeks occurred after the note released. Held or pending manual seek is outside the supported scope; do not describe intended ruler targets as measured targets.

rows.evidence: Run05 fixes an observed initial-activation latency restart ordering defect; subsequent accelerated offline exports complete. Runs21/24 preserve ordering, D, pitch and identity offline.
rows.limit: Use the fixed wrapper ordering and documented tested host configuration. RT/offline reactivation creates shared positive raw counter gaps and fresh generations; it is not uninterrupted processing.

rows.evidence: Run24 isolated B with64-sample limiter and configured+64: tuner output lies64samples before input song time on hub timeline, limiter restores nominal time, both WAVs first become nonzero1sample after each nominal onset.
rows.limit: This is one known branch latency. Time Shift's intentional advance in run09 is a separate manipulation and must not be called ordinary effect compensation.

rows.case: Valid late reply and queued event stream
rows.evidence: Runs07/15/16: intentional miss is diagnosed; output begins at first legal callback after visibility. Run16 receives release, three pitch expressions and CC before answer; accepted output preserves whole-stream timing and note duration.
rows.limit: Apparatus extra-shift policy is not a production retiming contract. CC timing/type are traced; controller/value bytes are not.

rows.evidence: Runs13/17: silent or muted/soloed live sources keep complete intervals. Run13 preserves the held lifetime across mute/solo without MIDI retrigger. Run20 returns CONTINUE_IF_NOT_QUIET but remains continuously scheduled through silent stopped periods.
rows.limit: Actual host sleep and wake were not observed. Keep-alive is an explicit supported-configuration requirement; missing callbacks cannot be inferred as silence.

rows.evidence: Runs11/12/14/17: fresh generations and independently timed rejoin; held downstream signal extinguishes on measured bypass/removal. Pending reset cancels old events and does not resurrect an attack when the missing source returns.
rows.limit: Only the tested reset/activation routes are supported. Numeric downstream silence does not reveal the host/instrument's private voice termination mechanism.

rows.evidence: Run15:1025 stopped-transport blocks remain nonzero until translated NoteOff; first zero is24.125292s after stop. Bypass/removal behaved differently.
rows.limit: BLOCKER before #616: resolve #632 explicit stop cancellation of pending and held voices, reply invalidation and return to normal D. Do not silently adopt whole-stream translation as the production stop policy.

rows.case: Pitch, expression composition and note identity
rows.evidence: Run21 RT/offline each forwards3103 changing expressions as exact f32(input+.5), ordered at D; isolated Polysynth audio follows75→175c. Run24 isolated Vital early/sustained pitch is approximately+50.10c in RT/offline. Explicit attack IDs and injected tuning IDs match; source identity separates reused IDs.
rows.limit: Windowed spectral measurements do not prove the first individual audio sample's pitch. Vital requires the tested MPE/range configuration. Releases can carry wildcard note_id=-1.

rows.evidence: Run23 attempted overlap arrives already serialized: raw off(-1) before each replacement on, preserved as off→on→same-ID tuning at D. Editor-free runs and shared-PID/reload evidence are retained in the archives.
rows.limit: Actual overlapping same-key lifetimes never reached the tuner, so overlap support remains excluded. No upstream control trace identifies the source of retrigger termination. Shared-process restrictions still apply.
